subject: Queue harmonics: stabilization plan and customer communication
messages:
From: Elena Parkel <ep@novatrade.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spikes + throughput drop (novatrade-prod)

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

We're seeing repeating p95 latency spikes and a ~30% drop in sustained throughput across our checkout inference calls since ~08:45 PDT. Attached is a short graph from our telemetry showing three distinct spike clusters between 08:45-09:05. Keys:
- Endpoint: genapi.redwood/v1/complete (model: rwd-gpt-large)
- Symptoms: p95 from ~180ms -> 1.2s, overall QPS down from 420 -> ~290
- We already scaled our client-side concurrency down to 60% with no stable effect

This is impacting payment flow (order confirmation timeouts reported by customers). Can you confirm this is on your side and share immediate mitigation options? We're happy to provide a maintenance window if you need short routing changes.

Attachments: qps-spike-23jul.pdf

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Parkel
SRE, NovaTrade
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Parkel <ep@novatrade.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 09:18:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spikes + throughput drop (novatrade-prod)

Thanks for the heads up, Elena — and sorry for the disruption.

Short summary of next steps (triage in progress):
1) Karthik/SRE: please run a targeted canary against the affected routing slice and check queue depth + partition hotness.
2) CS (Marissa): we need to draft a one‑paragraph customer-facing brief with what we know + actions and propose a maintenance window.
3) Product (Grace): quick decision on whether we should activate protective routing to Dedicated pool for NovaTrade while we stabilize.

Karthik — tagging you for live triage. If SRE confirms a hot partition or queue oscillation, propose the short-term mitigations (routing to dedicated pool, reducing aggressive client-side retries, lowering model max_tokens for in-flight calls).

I'll consolidate and send a single customer-facing note once we have the canary snapshot (ETA ~20m).

— Mateo Alvarez
TPM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spikes + throughput drop (novatrade-prod)

On Mon, Jul 23, 2028 at 9:18 AM mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Karthik — tagging you for live triage. If SRE confirms a hot partition or queue oscillation, propose the short-term mitigations (routing to dedicated pool, reducing aggressive client-side retries, lowering model max_tokens for in-flight calls).

Quick initial findings from the canary run (attached canary-results-23jul.csv):
- Observed a recurring queue depth oscillation on instance-set a9 (avg qdepth burst to 512 then fall to ~40 every ~90s).
- CPU/KV cache heat pattern shows local KV misses during bursts -> small but compounding generation stall.
- Traces show a cluster of calls with repeated client retries that line up with the burst windows (likely amplifying the oscillation).

Short-term mitigations (recommended, ordered):
1) Protective routing: shift NovaTrade traffic for 30m to a lightly loaded dedicated pool (manual route rule). Low risk, immediate impact.
2) Enable KV warmup for the dedicated pool and pre-warm common prefixes (reduces miss penalty).
3) Recommend NovaTrade reduce client retries (max backoff -> 3s, cap attempts at 2) until we finish stabilization.
4) If routing is not possible, apply a transient max_tokens cap of 256 on front-line calls to limit per-request compute.

We can implement 1+2 in ~10 minutes if product signs off for the dedicated route. I'll prepare a short rollback plan and include telemetry check scripts.

Attaching: canary-results-23jul.csv (summary table + qdepth timeline)

— Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: mateo_alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Parkel <ep@novatrade.com>, Rajesh Singh <rajesh@novatrade.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: [Redwood] Immediate mitigation plan and 11:00 maintenance window request (novatrade-prod)

Elena / Rajesh —

Thanks again for flagging this. Short customer-facing summary and ask:

What happened:
- We observed queue depth oscillations on our serving fleet that correlate with repeated client retries. Those oscillations produce transient KV miss patterns and per-request stalls, causing p95 to spike and sustained throughput to drop.

What we are doing (next 30m):
- Shift NovaTrade routing to a lightly loaded dedicated pool to break the oscillation and restore throughput (30m test).
- Enable KV warmup and pre-warming for common prefixes on the dedicated pool.
- Request NovaTrade temporarily cap client retries (2 attempts, exponential backoff starting at 250ms) to reduce amplification while we validate.

Customer ask / window:
- Can you approve a short maintenance window at 11:00–11:15 PDT for the routing change? The change is non-disruptive; we will run checks and alert you at +5m / +15m.

Rollback:
- If we see unexpected behavior, we will revert routing and reapply conservative throttle rules. Expect <10m rollback.

Attachments: customer-brief-23jul.md (one‑paragraph summary + timeline), canary-results-23jul.csv, qps-spike-23jul.pdf

I'll remain on this thread during the window and will share telemetry snapshots at +5/+15.

— Mateo Alvarez
TPM, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
